decision.explanation: REVISIONS. 1) The source supports ponatinib activity against BCR-ABL with ABL1 T315I in CML: it states ponatinib is the only approved TKI capable of inhibiting BCR-ABL with the gatekeeper T315I mutation and that T315I is associated with resistant or relapsed CML [pmid-25349473:f01]. 2) The PACE excerpt provides observed response evidence, reporting major cytogenetic response in 74% of patients with the T315I mutant, but the excerpt does not explicitly restrict that response figure to CML-only patients because the trial also included Ph+ALL [pmid-25349473:f02]. 3) The claim as written includes variantOrigin=SOMATIC, but the supplied excerpts do not explicitly state that BCR::ABL1 or ABL1 T315I is somatic; the CML resistance context suggests acquired origin but does not establish it. Therefore the claim is partially supported and should be revised to qualify or remove the somatic-origin assertion and to avoid treating the PACE T315I response rate as CML-only unless further specified.

citations.quote: Ponatinib is the only approved TKI capable of inhibiting BCR-ABL with the gatekeeper T315I kinase domain mutation, known to be the cause for 20% of resistant or relapsed CML cases. . . . Although the overall structure remains similar in many ways to other approved TKIs, the ability to potently inhibit native BCR-ABL, BCR-ABL-T315I, and many other mutant forms of BCR-ABL made ponatinib a highly versatile drug with great potential moving into clinical evaluation. . . .

The Phase II Ponatinib Ph+ALL and CML Evaluation (PACE) trial enrolled 449 patients: 267 with CP-CML, 83 with accelerated phase (AP)-CML, and 94 with blast crisis (BC)-CML or Ph+ALL . . . Responses were observed for each of 15 mutations present at baseline for CP-CML patients, and 26 unique mutations in total. Response rates were similar for those with and without mutant BCR-ABL, with MCyR occurring in 56% of all patients, 49% of patients with native BCR-ABL, 64% for those with one mutation, 62% for those with two or more mutations, and 74% for those with the T315I mutant. . . .

unresolved: Somatic origin of BCR::ABL1/ABL1 T315I is not explicitly stated in the supplied excerpts; the CML resistance context suggests but does not establish it.
The PACE 74% MCyR figure for T315I mutant patients is not explicitly restricted to CML-only patients in the supplied excerpt.
